title: Direct image of an injective module is acyclic for object evaluation on a ringed site
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $f:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be a morphism of sites presented by a continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, and let $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C},\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}$ be sheaves of rings with a map $\rho:\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}\to f_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}$. Direct image of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] means $(f_*I)(U)=I(u(U))$ with scalar action through $\rho_U$. Assume both module categories have enough injectives [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and all objects, arrows, coefficients and covering index sets lie in a common universe. If $I$ is an injective $\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}$-module, then for every object $U$ of $\mathcal C$ and every integer $q>0$,
$$R^q\Gamma(U,-)(f_*I)=0,$$
where $\Gamma(U,-):\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal C,\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})\to\mathrm{Ab}$ is the additive left exact evaluation functor $P\mapsto P(U)$ and its right derived functors are computed in the module category by injective resolutions. No flatness of $\rho$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 072Z, label lemma-direct-image-injective-sheaf (direct image is totally acyclic), and Tag 0731, label lemma-limp-acyclic (1) (acyclic for object evaluation).

proof.text: Put $P=f_*I$ and forget its scalar action. For a covering $\mathcal V=\{V_j\to V\}$ of $\mathcal C$, continuity of $u$ carries it to the covering $u\mathcal V=\{u(V_j)\to u(V)\}$ of $\mathcal D$. Its covering-base-change comparison identifies $u(V_{j_0}\times_V\cdots\times_VV_{j_p})$ with $u(V_{j_0})\times_{u(V)}\cdots\times_{u(V)}u(V_{j_p})$ by induction on $p$. The isomorphisms preserve each tuple projection, since each comparison is characterized by its projections. Apply the contravariant restriction maps of $I$ to these comparisons, component by component, and take products. This gives an isomorphism $\check C^\bullet(\mathcal V,P_{ab})\cong\check C^\bullet(u\mathcal V,I_{ab})$: both differentials are the same alternating sum of restrictions along the projections omitting one index. The ring map $\rho$ only supplies the scalar action on $P$ and does not enter this additive complex.

source.place: Tag 072Z, label lemma-direct-image-injective-sheaf, second paragraph of proof; continuity is Sites Tag 00WV

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-injective-module-cech-acyclic] to $I$ and $u\mathcal V$. The site axioms and common universe are precisely its precoverage and size hypotheses. In the usual abelian sheaf categories on these small sites, sheafification is the exact sheafification of [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]; and [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-iso-locally-bijective] states that a presheaf map is inverted by abelian sheafification exactly when it is locally injective and locally surjective. This is precisely the WEqualsLocallyBijective condition; thus both sheafification hypotheses are supplied by cited statements. Hence $\check H^p(u\mathcal V,I_{ab})=0$ for $p>0$, and the complex isomorphism of step 1 gives $\check H^p(\mathcal V,P_{ab})=0$ for every covering $\mathcal V$ and $p>0$.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-site-cech-vanishing-criterion] on $\mathcal C$ with $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ and $\mathrm{Cov}=\operatorname{Cov}(\mathcal C)$. Condition (1) holds because every covering intersection is an object of the site; condition (2) holds because each covering refines itself by the identity arrows; condition (3) is step 2. It follows that $H^q(U,P_{ab})=0$ for every $U$ and $q>0$.

source.place: Tag 03F9, label lemma-cech-vanish-collection; Tag 072Z, final sentence of proof

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison] to the $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$-module $P=f_*I$. The common universe and enough-injectives hypotheses are those of the item. Its comparison gives $R^q\Gamma(U,-)(f_*I)\cong H^q(U,P_{ab})=0$ for every $q>0$, proving the required module-category derived vanishing. No step uses exactness of extension of scalars or claims that $f_*I$ is injective, so no flatness of $\rho$ is needed.
